CAT.rationale: Caterpillar's fundamental health and trajectory are mixed: strong YoY revenue (+22.2%) and EPS (+30.2%) growth, a record $51-63B backlog, and a best-in-class franchise with unmatched dealer network and growing services revenue ($24B in 2025, targeting $28B in 2026). However, margins are compressing (gross margin 35.1% vs 37.0% YoY, operating margin 17.7% vs 18.1%), operating cash flow is volatile and fell 50% QoQ to $1.87B, and balance-sheet leverage is rising (D/E 4.12x vs 3.70x a year prior). The franchise quality is real but the trajectory is deteriorating at the margin level. Pillar 2 is decisively negative: the P/E has tripled from 16.8x to 46.5x — the absolute top of its 365-day range — while net margin has slipped from 15.7% to 13.3% and ROE from 55% to 50.5%. The earnings yield of 2.2% sits 227bps below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.47%, implying a deeply negative equity-risk premium. The stock has tripled from its 52-week low ($345.85 to $940.48) on multiple expansion, not fundamental improvement. Pillar 3 offers no offset: $2.2-2.4B in tariff headwinds for 2026 ($710M in Q1 alone), China macro softness (fixed-asset investment contraction, slowest industrial production growth in nearly three years), and insider sales in May 2026 are near-term downside catalysts. The Supreme Court tariff refund ($1.5-1.8B) is a potential positive but uncertain in timing. Any earnings miss or multiple normalization toward the 1-year median (~25-27x P/E) implies 40-45% downside. All three pillars align negatively: deteriorating margins, extreme overvaluation vs own history, and tangible near-term headwinds.
